title: China proposes licensing limits on exports of advanced AI technology
dek: Draft rules distinguish overseas access to Chinese AI services from exporting underlying models, data and know-how.
evidence: Reuters analysis of draft Chinese regulations; not final law
takeaway: Evaluate portability of model weights, hosting rights and know-how transfers separately from ordinary API availability.

sections.title: Draft scope

bullets.detail: The proposals would allow many overseas customers to consume hosted Chinese AI, while requiring approval for certain transfers of models, data, advanced agents and related technology.
Reuters reports 23 technologies added to proposed control lists, with additional attention to large-scale compute operations, model capability thresholds and ownership transfers.

paragraphs: Transfer boundary: The proposals would allow many overseas customers to consume hosted Chinese AI, while requiring approval for certain transfers of models, data, advanced agents and related technology.
Scope: Reuters reports 23 technologies added to proposed control lists, with additional attention to large-scale compute operations, model capability thresholds and ownership transfers.

sections.title: What changes

bullets.detail: The measures are proposals, with comments due November 15, and their implementation and definitions may change before adoption.
Map models by provenance, weight custody, inference location, hosting terms and fallback options; distinguish SaaS access from exportable deployment artifacts.

paragraphs: Uncertainty: The measures are proposals, with comments due November 15, and their implementation and definitions may change before adoption.
